field.title: Owner Side
field.description: The parent side of the relationship: the lifecycle owner, and the end without the foreign key. Derived from relationship_type for one_to_many (source) and many_to_one (target). Set by hand only for one_to_one.

entity.description: The canonical entity-relationship graph between data objects, independent of any specific solution's implementation. Captures directed relationships like User owns Asset (1:N, composition), Customer places Order (1:N, reference), Employee works on Project (M:N, association), Customer is a Person (1:1, inheritance). Carries both cardinality (Cardinality) and structural kind (Kind) so the catalog distinguishes ownership from loose reference from peer association from subtype. Self-references are allowed (User directly manages User).

computed_fields.name: data_object_relationship_label
computed_fields.description: Composed from the source data object name, the relationship verb, and the target data object name. Recomputed on every write so renames in either parent flow through.

computed_fields.name: owner_side
computed_fields.description: The parent side is the one side of the cardinality, so it is derived and cannot disagree with it. Kept as written for one_to_one and many_to_many, where cardinality does not decide it.

validation_rules.name: users_relationship_is_not_many_to_many_reference
validation_rules.message: A reference to users is one person per record. Use one one_to_many relationship from users for each kind of person, or a junction entity or an association for a genuine panel or team.
validation_rules.description: Check B7b. A row-scope rule needs a single owner, and each relationship to users holds one person.

validation_rules.name: persona_only_on_users_relationship
validation_rules.message: Only a relationship to users can name a persona.
validation_rules.description: The persona is the kind of person who fills this relationship to users.
